items.followUp: Define the infectious period of a disease.

rubric.why: Identifies the start and duration of the incubation period.
rubric.description: States that the incubation period is a time interval beginning when a pathogen enters the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the interval from pathogen entry.

rubric.why: Identifies when the incubation period ends.
rubric.description: States that the interval ends when disease symptoms appear.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the appearance of symptoms as the endpoint.

modelAnswer: The incubation period is the time between the entry of a pathogen into the body and the appearance of disease symptoms.

items.followUp: Define a scientific theory and give one example.

rubric.why: Assesses the definition of a law or principle.
rubric.description: Defines a law or principle as a general statement describing a particular relationship under given conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition containing this idea.

rubric.why: Assesses whether two examples are given.
rubric.description: Gives two examples: the law of dominance and the law of segregation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both examples.

modelAnswer: A law or principle is a general statement describing a particular relationship under given conditions.
Examples are Mendel's law of dominance and law of segregation.

items.followUp: State two functions of stomata in leaves.

rubric.why: Assesses one valid function of epidermal tissue.
rubric.description: States that epidermal tissue protects the plant from injury and infection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this protective function.

rubric.why: Assesses a second function associated with epidermal tissue.
rubric.description: States that stomata in the epidermis allow gas exchange.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying gas exchange as a function.

modelAnswer: Epidermal tissue protects the plant from injury and infection.
It reduces water loss; stomata in the epidermis allow gas exchange.

items.followUp: What is meant by a vulnerable species?

rubric.description: Defines an extinct species as one with no living members remaining.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that no living members of the species remain.

rubric.description: Defines an endangered species as one at risk of extinction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the species is at risk of extinction.

modelAnswer: An extinct species has no living members remaining.
An endangered species is one that is at risk of extinction.
